name: Auramaxxing

lead: Auramaxxing is slang for working to maximize one's 'aura', meaning stylishness and a charismatic presence. It is a social-media-driven trend that treats presentation (grooming, clothes, composure) as something you can improve.

'Aura points' are an informal joke scoring system: users award or deduct imaginary points for everyday moments, such as gaining them by acting confidently or losing them by an embarrassing slip. The scores have no real meaning and are mostly not tallied.

paras: Practitioners describe it as improving self-presentation: grooming, dress, confident body language and composure. There is no fixed method.
No physical risks. Commentators, including Thred citing an author in The Cut, have criticized some auramaxxing content as heavily gendered or misogynistic.

chain: Pay attention to grooming, dress and demeanor
angle.text: Auramaxxing is about perceived coolness rather than a specific physical trait. People pursue it by improving how they present themselves and carry themselves.

lead: Auramaxxing is internet slang for trying to raise one's 'aura', a term for stylishness and confident, suave excellence. It applies the looksmaxxing suffix '-maxxing' to a charisma concept, especially through grooming, dress and other self-presentation among younger men.

The word 'aura' began as football fan slang: fans of Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk started using it around 2020, then it spread to praising charismatic figures generally. In May 2024, TikTok users popularized 'aura points', a running joke that quantifies social behavior [1].

paras: According to Know Your Meme, fans of Virgil van Dijk used 'aura' around 2020, citing a New York Times article quoting him; use spread to other figures in 2023, and teens on TikTok began the aura points gag in May 2024 [1]. Examples include losing points for an unzipped backpack or a loud stomach rumble in class [1].
Some outlets describe auramaxxing content as often containing gendered advice, and Thred, quoting a writer cited from The Cut, has said it is rife with misogyny [2].

timeline.event: Van Dijk fans begin saying he has 'aura' [1].
